sermons.life_context: He had been sole minister of Westminster Chapel in London since G. Campbell Morgan retired in 1943. In 1950 he also started the annual Puritan Conference at the chapel with J. I. Packer and O. Raymond Johnston.

He was sole minister of Westminster Chapel in London. The series came just before his Sunday-morning Ephesians exposition, which began on 3 October 1954. In his own account, quoted from Iain Murray's biography, he felt he had to preach these sermons before moving on to Ephesians.

Throughout these years he was sole minister of Westminster Chapel in London. From October 1955 he also preached through Romans on Friday evenings while this Sunday-morning series continued. In 1959 he paused Ephesians to preach on revival.

The series covers his later years as sole minister of Westminster Chapel. It ran alongside his Sunday-morning Ephesians series until 1962 and his Sunday-evening Acts series from 1965, and it spanned his October 1966 call for evangelicals to leave mixed denominations. It ended in March 1968, when, by his own account, major surgery led him to leave the chapel; he retired that year.

He was sole minister of Westminster Chapel in London, preaching Ephesians on Sunday mornings and Romans on Friday evenings. According to the MLJ Trust, he broke off the Ephesians series for these sermons because he considered the subject urgent.
He was sole minister of Westminster Chapel in London. His Sunday-morning Ephesians series had ended in 1962, and his Friday-evening exposition of Romans was still running at the chapel.

He had retired from Westminster Chapel in 1968, after major surgery that March, and was editing his sermons for publication. The MLJ Trust says retirement let him accept the seminary's longstanding invitation, which his weekly preaching had previously ruled out.

He was sole minister of Westminster Chapel in London, preaching through Ephesians on Sunday mornings and Romans on Friday evenings. The year before, he had paused the Ephesians series to preach on revival.

He was sole minister of Westminster Chapel in London and was also preaching through Acts on Sunday evenings. The sermon came about four and a half months after his 18 October 1966 address urging evangelicals to leave mixed denominations, which John Stott publicly disputed.

He was sole minister of Westminster Chapel in London, but the MLJ Trust does not name where this sermon was preached. It came two weeks before his Sunday-morning Ephesians series began on 3 October 1954.

He was sole minister of Westminster Chapel in London, preaching Romans on Friday evenings and Acts on Sunday evenings. The sermon came just over three weeks after his 18 October 1966 address to the National Assembly of Evangelicals, where the chairman, John Stott, publicly disagreed with his call to leave mixed denominations.

He was sole minister of Westminster Chapel in London. In October 1955, a few months before this sermon, he had started a Friday-evening exposition of Romans at the chapel, which ran alongside this Sunday-morning Ephesians series.
He was sole minister of Westminster Chapel in London, in the first year of his Sunday-evening Acts series (1965–1968). His Friday-evening exposition of Romans was still running at the chapel.
He gave the address on 18 October 1966 at Westminster Central Hall. At the time he was sole minister of Westminster Chapel, preaching Romans on Friday evenings and Acts on Sunday evenings.
